 South Africa South Africa’s diesel price to drop, petrol little changed after levy cut
 Sfundo Parakozov and Nilutpal Timsina By Reuters Published November 3, 2026 at 11:56 GMT Save Share 
 A petrol station attendant fills up a car ahead of a petrol price increase effective from midnight, at a filling station in Johannesburg, South Africa, May 31, 2022. REUTERS/Siphiwe Sibeko 
 JOHANNESBURG, Nov 3 (Reuters) – South Africa’s diesel price will fall in November while petrol will be little changed after the government announced fuel-tax cuts in a mid-year budget review.
 The wholesale diesel price will fall by up to 1.20 rand ($0.0722) a litre from November 4, while the regulated petrol price will decline by 1 cent a litre, the petroleum department said on Tuesday, announcing monthly price adjustments.
 The finance minister announced the tax cuts last month, cutting the fuel levy by 3 rand per litre for diesel and 1.50 rand per litre for petrol from November 4 to December 1.
 Smaller levy reductions will be in place until January 5, part of efforts to ease cost-of-living pressures on households and businesses.
 The petroleum department said in a statement that higher crude oil and petroleum product prices and a weaker rand currency contributed to November’s fuel price adjustments.
 South Africa imports most of its fuel, leaving it vulnerable to fluctuations in global energy prices.
 ($1 = 16.6236 rand)
